Distributing a package that uses RZig

Source: vignettes/distributing.Rmd
distributing.Rmd

A package that uses RZig is a source package with compiled code: whoever installs it from source needs R’s build tools and a Zig compiler of the supported series (0.16 or 0.17). rzig itself is pure R and needs no compiler. This vignette describes what a package states about Zig, how users obtain the compiler, and the channels through which such a package reaches its users. The code is plain R.

What the package states

create_rzig_package() and use_rzig() write the field that names the compiler, and rzig_status() notes a DESCRIPTION without it:

path <- file.path(tempdir(), "distpkg")
create_rzig_package(path, tests = FALSE)
#> Created package distpkg at /tmp/RtmpbmQ3hi/distpkg
#> Write Zig functions in src/rzig/src/main.zig, then run rzig::document(path) and rzig::build_zig(path)
read.dcf(file.path(path, "DESCRIPTION"), fields = "SystemRequirements")
#>      SystemRequirements    
#> [1,] "Zig 0.16.x or 0.17.x"

configure reports the compiler it uses in the installation log and rejects other versions with a message that names the version it found, and the Zig build uses at most two jobs, as CRAN’s policy for compiled code asks.

How users get Zig

find_zig() reports the compiler that an installation would use. A user without one installs a verified release with install_zig(), which asks for permission, downloads the archive of a pinned release, checks its SHA-256 checksum and keeps it in the user cache folder of rzig, where configure finds it:

find_zig(required = FALSE)
#> Zig compiler: /home/runner/work/_temp/9e0fe227-0da4-4767-900a-44012cf37f43/zig-x86_64-linux-0.16.0/zig (version 0.16.0, supported)
#> rzig supports Zig 0.16.x or 0.17.x.

Alternatives are a download from https://ziglang.org/download/, with the compiler on PATH or named by ZIG, or RZIG_DOWNLOAD_ZIG=true in the environment of the installation, with which configure downloads and checks the same pinned release itself when it finds no compiler.

GitHub and r-universe

remotes::install_github() and pak::pak() build the package from source on the user’s machine, so the user needs Zig as above. r-universe builds binary packages for Windows and macOS on its own machines, which have no Zig; a package for r-universe or GitHub can ask configure to download the pinned release into its build folder when no compiler is found:

cat("Config/rzig/download-zig: true\n", file = file.path(path, "DESCRIPTION"), append = TRUE)
status <- rzig_status(path)
status[status$step == "DESCRIPTION", ]
#> RZig status of package distpkg
#>   [ok] DESCRIPTION   package distpkg
#>                      Config/rzig/download-zig: configure downloads a verified
#>                        Zig when it finds none; CRAN does not allow that without
#>                        its consent, so a package for CRAN leaves the field out

The download goes to src/rzig/.zig-download, which the build excludes from the package and cleanup removes. Users of binary packages need no compiler at all.

CRAN

CRAN’s build machines have no Zig compiler, and CRAN’s policy forbids downloading a compiler during the installation without the agreement of the CRAN team, so Config/rzig/download-zig is not for packages on CRAN. A package for CRAN states Zig in SystemRequirements, as packages with Rust code state Cargo; whether CRAN builds such packages depends on CRAN providing the compiler. rzig itself is on CRAN because its checks compile no Zig code.

Continuous integration

use_rzig_ci() writes a GitHub Actions workflow that installs Zig 0.16 and 0.17 and runs R CMD check with the settings that CRAN applies to compiled code on Linux, macOS and Windows:

use_rzig_ci(path)
#> Wrote .github/workflows/rzig-check.yaml for package distpkg
file.exists(file.path(path, ".github", "workflows", "rzig-check.yaml"))
#> [1] TRUE
